clue.text: Alfred gave a seaman a sudden fright

parts.note: Al is the short form of the name Alfred
RM stands for Royal Marine, a sea-going serviceman

explanation.surface: A man called Alfred startles a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gave' is only a link between the wordplay and the definition. RM (Royal Marine) is the British corps of naval infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: A scare or shock of sudden fear is an everyday synonym.

clue.text: Star rose to become a champion defender

indicators.note: the letters of the two words turn into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity's rise turns them into a great advocate.
explanation.walkthrough: STAR ROSE, rearranged as signalled by 'to become', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who asserts a cause is its champion, standing up to defend it.

clue.text: Area where a native American located precious metal

indicators.note: the metal is found placed within the tribe's name, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the Cree are a native people of North America
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Asks where an indigenous American found gold or silver.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cree are a people of Canada and the northern US plains; 'where' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Land measured in acres is an expanse of ground, its extent or size.

clue.text: A kind team companion

indicators.note: kind means a sort, and to sort letters is to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A friendly group of fellow players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind' reads as gentle, but in the sense 'sort' it signals reordering TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal or friend, in British usage especially.

clue.text: Rhubarb!

parts.note: rhubarb is the word actors mutter to sound like background chatter, and so means meaningless talk or nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive words for empty, meaningless chatter.

clue.text: Exotic trollop remands British statesman

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so these letters are given an unfamiliar new order

explanation.surface: An exotic loose woman sends a politician back into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: TROLLOP REMANDS, rearranged as 'Exotic' signals, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian prime minister Henry Temple, 3rd Viscount, was known by this title.

clue.text: Draw a veil over mask

definitions.meaning: to keep something out of sight or not speak of it

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean conceal: to keep a matter quiet and to cover something up.

clue.text: Brief the French against being in charge

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Briefing that the French oppose taking command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse, using few words, as the Spartans of Laconia were said to speak.

clue.text: Surround with a hard rim

parts.note: H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard
an edge is a rim or border

explanation.surface: Instructions to encircle something with a tough border.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring a field with shrubs, hence to enclose or hem in.

clue.text: Coaching combinations of communicating compartments

parts.note: railway coaches joined together, whose compartments open onto a shared passage running along the side

explanation.surface: Sounds like a training scheme for sports teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coaching' suggests training; it means made up of railway coaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Trains with a side passage linking every compartment of the carriages.

clue.text: Music for animals overeating trout ultimately

indicators.note: eating means the reversed animals swallow a letter, which goes inside them
over signals turning the word for the animals back to front

parts.note: otters are river animals

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word trout

explanation.surface: A tune written for creatures that gorge on trout.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'overeating' into 'over' and 'eating': 'over' turns OTTERS into SRETTO, and 'eating' puts T (last of trout) inside it. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fugue, the overlapping entry of voices is a musical term from Italian for narrow.

clue.text: Benito in communist guise lost weight

indicators.note: in places the dictator's title within the word for a communist

parts.note: a Red is a communist
Benito Mussolini was called Il Duce, the leader

explanation.surface: Mussolini disguised as a communist slimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: Mussolini styled himself Il Duce, 'the leader'; 'guise' is only part of the link and adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Slimmed or shed pounds, as a dieter cuts their mass.

clue.text: Non-imaginary number

definitions.meaning: in mathematics any figure with no imaginary part belongs to this class of numbers

explanation.definitionFit: Genuine or actual, and also a figure on the continuous line of numbers in mathematics.

clue.text: Fall over the last piece of rubbish

parts.note: to trip is to stumble or fall

indicators.note: the final letter of the word that follows is all that is taken

explanation.surface: Tumbling over the final scrap of refuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense, worthless talk; the word also names cow's stomach eaten as food.

clue.text: In contact with religion on one occasion only

parts.note: on means touching or in contact, as a switch that is on
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Touching faith just a single time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A single time and no more.

clue.text: Bird in a group perches in the trees — it takes off later

indicators.note: the bird is said to sit inside the words that follow, so its name lies concealed within them

explanation.surface: A bird in a flock sits up in the branches before flying away.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'treeS — IT TAkes'. 'in a group' makes the definition a genus, the scientific grouping of the nuthatches; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin genus name of the nuthatches, small birds that clamber about tree trunks.

clue.text: Stave off a match

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or spoiled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: To fend off a contest or game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stave off' reads as a phrase meaning repel; 'off' is the anagram signal for STAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A short wax friction light, named after the Roman goddess of the hearth.

clue.text: Extra fulfilment by consuming too much

parts.note: over means extra or in excess, as in left over
an indulgence is a gratification of a desire

explanation.surface: Satisfaction beyond what is needed comes from excess eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess in eating or drinking, gluttony.

clue.text: Compound of 2 atoms of al, with I, k and ne is not acidic

indicators.note: a chemical compound combines elements, so these letters are mixed together

parts.note: two atoms of aluminium, chemical symbol Al, give the symbol twice over

explanation.surface: A chemistry formula of aluminium, iodine, potassium and neon that is a base.
explanation.walkthrough: AL twice with I and K, rearranged as 'Compound of' signals, makes ALKALI; NE follows. 'with' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a pH above seven, the chemical opposite of sour or corrosive acid.

clue.text: Person living on the district line, for example

definitions.text: Person living on the district line, for example

parts.words: Person living on the district line, for example
parts.note: the District line is a London Underground railway, so a dweller on it lives below the ground

explanation.surface: Someone whose home is near a particular London transport route.
explanation.walkthrough: The District line is one of London's Underground (subway) lines; read 'living on' it literally and the person lives beneath the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally below the ground, the realm of an Underground railway line.

clue.text: Principled noble

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean honest and morally sound, as a decent citizen is.

clue.text: Did Dr Jones live here in the USA?

definitions.text: Did Dr Jones live here in the USA?

parts.words: Did Dr Jones live here in the USA?
parts.note: the film archaeologist Dr Jones has a first name that is also a US state

explanation.surface: A query about where an American academic once resided.
explanation.walkthrough: Indiana Jones, the film hero, is called Dr Jones; his first name is also a Midwestern state.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern state that shares its name with the adventurer of the films.

clue.text: 'You are really naughty' starts the story

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter of each of the quoted words

explanation.surface: A scolding that begins a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, rambling tale, as a sailor might spin.

clue.text: Ex-pupil and boy come up with a lout

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: OB means old boy, a former pupil of a school
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy and a lad appear alongside a hooligan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come up' turns both pieces round together, as a down clue is read upwards; OB (old boy) is the British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a rough, uncouth young man, a hooligan.

clue.text: Common drug

definitions.meaning: as a noun, a common is open public land covered in turf

explanation.definitionFit: A village common is grassland, and the word is also slang for marijuana.

clue.text: Even the middleman has an opinion

indicators.note: even points to the letters in the second, fourth, sixth and eighth places

explanation.surface: A go-between holds a view of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' and 'has' are links; take letters 2, 4, 6 and 8 of MIDDLEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or view held in the mind.

clue.text: Mite found on a moggy

parts.note: moggy is British slang for a cat, and a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A tiny parasite discovered on a pet cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found on' is a link: in this down clue A sits above TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny particle, the smallest bit of something.

clue.text: Endorsement for a small number to visit south Africa

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A stamp in the passport lets a few people travel to South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' and 'to visit' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp in a passport giving permission to enter a country.

clue.text: Bother a sober person — I then follow the car builder

parts.note: to bug someone is to bother them
TT is teetotal, a person who never drinks alcohol

explanation.surface: Pestering a teetotaller before following the motor manufacturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then follow' just strings the pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian-French maker of racing and luxury sports cars, founded by Ettore of that name.

clue.text: No apparatus required by French friend to practise far eastern art

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
a rig is a piece of equipment
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: No equipment is needed by a Frenchman's pal to pursue a craft from Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required by' and 'to practise' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: One of cheerful outlook mistakenly omits tip

indicators.note: mistakenly means the letters are set down wrongly and so need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone upbeat accidentally leaves out a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: OMITS TIP, rearranged as 'mistakenly' signals, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who always expects the best, a hopeful sort.

clue.text: To lower a number system

parts.note: a base, such as base ten or binary, is the root of a counting system

explanation.surface: Bringing down a way of counting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble or degrade someone, bringing them down in rank or esteem.
